text:
Dev Patel: Hey folks — for the incident taxonomy rollout, Support needs a clear “category -> playbook” mapping + what fields we should expect to be filled during an active escalation.

Dev Patel: Right now we get pulled into #inc- channels and half the time we don’t know if it’s routing vs capacity vs runtime. What will be required in the bot, and what can we count on for customer messaging?

Jasmine Liu: +1. For enterprise we need to know (a) impacted surface (Hosted vs Dedicated), (b) region, (c) whether it’s widespread vs single tenant, and (d) who’s actually owning updates. Otherwise our “ETA” is guesswork.

Rachel Kim: Also: are categories going to be stable enough to map to macros? I can build templates in Zendesk/Jira but I need to know the allowed values.

Rafael Mendes: Yep, this is exactly why we’re standardizing it. Plan is:
- Category + impacted surface + customer tier + region are required fields on incident declare (or at least within 15 min of declare)
- Owner team is auto-suggested from category + impacted service, but IC can override
- We’ll allow reclassification post-incident (postmortem) but the live category should be “good enough” for comms + escalation routing

Rafael Mendes: Fields Support should expect in the #inc channel topic / incident bot summary:
- Severity (existing Sev1-3)
- Category (new taxonomy)
- Impacted surface: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private (if Redwood-operated)
- Region(s)
- Customer tier: self-serve / dedicated / enterprise
- Primary owner: oncall rotation + escalation channel
- Current customer-facing status (Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved)

Miles Thornton: Adding: we’re trying to keep categories small and “decisionable” during an incident. More detailed contributing factors can be filled in the postmortem.

Miles Thornton: Draft category buckets we’re using for playbook mapping (top level):
1) Edge/Gateway/Streaming (disconnects, TLS, CDN, websocket/HTTP2 weirdness)
2) Routing/Policy/Control plane (smart-routing rules, fallback loops, bad config pushes)
3) Capacity exhaustion / Autoscaling (saturation, queueing, no GPUs available)
4) Fleet/Infra (GPU node failures, provisioning, driver issues)
5) Runtime crash / OOM / kernel regression
6) Model-specific degradation (one model/version unstable, quality regression, tokenizer mismatch)
7) Data plane dependencies (vector store/reranker dependency, rate limiting backend, etc)

Miles Thornton: (Security stays in Security IR — can still tag impacted surface/region but different process.)

Allison Grant: For allowed values: we’re going to publish the canonical list in the incident metadata standard and enforce via incident-bot dropdowns (no freeform). That’s so dashboards don’t turn into “routing”, “routing issue”, “router”, etc.

Rachel Kim: Great. Where will the category->playbook live? Ideally a single page we can link to from the #inc channel.

Rafael Mendes: Confluence page under Support escalation playbook. We’ll also link it directly from the incident bot modal (“Need help choosing? see playbook”) and from the #support-oncall runbook.

Jasmine Liu: Can we get guidance for what Support should do based on category? Like what questions we should ask IC, and what we should say to customers while we’re waiting.

Aisha Bello: We’re drafting “expected comms + SLA expectations” by (severity x category x tier). Not for customers verbatim, but for internal alignment.

Aisha Bello: For example:
- Sev1 Routing/Policy: fast mitigation target, frequent updates (every 15-30 min for enterprise), likely wide blast radius
- Sev1 Capacity exhaustion: mitigation may be scaling + shedding, comms should set expectation that ETAs depend on capacity add/route shift
- Sev1 Runtime crash: if there’s a rollback path, we do that; otherwise mitigation is model/version pinning or draining nodes

Dev Patel: Super helpful. For Support intake during an escalation, what should we ask the reporting customer to provide? We get “5xx/timeouts” and sometimes that’s all.

Mina Haddad: If it’s 5xx/timeouts, ask for:
- request_id / trace_id (if they have it)
- model name + version (if pinned)
- region endpoint they’re hitting
- whether it’s streaming vs non-streaming
- time window + approx RPS
We can usually separate Edge vs Routing vs Capacity pretty fast with those.

Irene Choi: For Dedicated specifically: add “pool name / deployment id” + “max_concurrency settings” if they have it. A lot of “platform down” reports are actually per-pool saturation.

Rachel Kim: Are we expecting IC to fill “impacted customers” or just tier? We can’t promise listing customers in the heat of the moment.

Rafael Mendes: Not required to list customers in the bot. Required is tier + whether it’s single-tenant vs multi-tenant if known. If it’s an enterprise customer, Support can add the account name in the Support thread / ticket, but we won’t make that a mandatory incident field.

Redwood Incident Bot: (preview) New required fields on /incident declare: Severity, Category, Impacted surface, Region, Customer tier. Optional: Impact summary, Suspected component/service. Owner team will be suggested automatically. :information_source:

Jasmine Liu: Re: updates — can we make “next update ETA” consistent? That’s the #1 thing CSMs ask for.

Rafael Mendes: Yes. We’re adding a “next update in X min” expectation to the IC checklist. For Sev1, default is 30 minutes unless stated otherwise.

Dev Patel: Ok, action items from Support side:
1) We’ll review the category->playbook mapping once you drop the link
2) We’ll update our macros/templates per category (Hosted vs Dedicated differences)
3) We’ll tell CSMs the minimum info to collect (request_id/model/region/streaming)

Miles Thornton: I’ll post the draft mapping here for feedback before we lock it. Biggest open question is whether “capacity exhaustion” and “routing overload” are separate in the playbook or merged. (Eng wants separate; Support may want them combined for comms.)

Rachel Kim: Separate is fine as long as the customer message guidance doesn’t diverge too much. We mostly need to know “is this scaling/queueing” vs “is this config/route selection.”

Aisha Bello: We can make the customer-facing guidance similar (“we’re mitigating elevated errors/latency”), but keep internal escalation distinct so the right team gets paged.

Dev Patel: Sounds good. Ping me when the Confluence page is live and I’ll route to Support leads for sign-off. :thumbsup: (reaction)
